featured_reviews.name: DINO NEIL D'MONTE
featured_reviews.review_text:
Blessed  ST Mother Teresa Church in Virar -- the only one in Maharashtra to be named after the nun .........................FEEL PROUD  PEOPLE !

Mother Teresa :

Peace begins with a smile..
Spread love everywhere you go. Let no one ever come to you without leaving happier.
If we have no peace, it is because we have forgotten that we belong to each other.
Let us always meet each other with smile, for the smile is the beginning of love.
There are no great things, only small things with great love. Happy are those.
Yesterday is gone. Tomorrow has not yet come. We have only today. Let us begin.
Love begins at home, and it is not how much we do... but how much love we put in that action.
If you judge people, you have no time to love them.
I have found the paradox that if I love until it hurts, then there is no hurt, but only more love.
If you can't feed a hundred people, then feed just one.

featured_reviews.name: Alphonsa Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text: It is a newly built Church for the Catholic Faithful in Virar west area. There is another RC church for Virar east faithful. The Church is located a little distant from the railway station noise and so is a preferred place for devotion and meditation. The Priests reside there so there is someone always available for you at all times. Morning mass at 7.30am and evening at 7pm (Mon to Sat). Sunday evening mass at 5pm. Not so sure about morning mass timings on Sunday. There is sufficient seating space for a crowd of approx 400 pax I guess. Accoustics and Church architect is pretty practical and yet very elegant. It is one of the few Churches dedicated to St Mother Teresa in India. It has a beautiful life like statue of Mother Teresa and a well thought of Altar with the virtues of Mother Teresa. You can reach the Church by rickshaw or walk from the Virar railway station for around 15mins.

customer_updates.name: Collins Furtado
customer_updates.text:
Holy Spirit Church

in Nandakhal, Virar West, is a historic Roman Catholic church built by the Portuguese Franciscans in 1573. It is the oldest church in North Vasai and one of the few in the region to have escaped destruction during the Maratha invasion of 1739.

Location & Hours

Address: CQQM+J8W, Nalla - Nandakhal Rd, Torbhat, Nandakhal, Virar West, Virar, Maharashtra.

History: The church was dedicated to the Holy Spirit and built to serve the increasing number of local Christian converts at the time. The original Portuguese architecture has been largely retained despite reconditioning and additions like a porch in the early 20th century.

featured_reviews.name: Cedric Noronha
featured_reviews.review_text: A historic Roman Catholic Church located at Nandakhal village in Virar. It was built by the Portuguese Franciscans in 1573. Escaping the Maratha destruction in 1739, this church is the oldest in North Vasai and is dedicated to the Holy Ghost. Its interior is simple having wooden pews, windows, gold guided altar, side altars, lofts etc. Above the  barrel vaulted ceiling is a fresco depicting the Holy Ghost. The facade of this church had two belfry towers on either side. Outside the church are tombstones, a cross stand and an artificial lake nearby. Had attended a mass service in this church in Marathi language. It is an ideal place for local devotees as well as people of other faith.

featured_reviews.name: Pius Lopes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Church of St. Roque
Erected in 1943 (ref: Catholic Diocese of Vasai)

History can safely record that this parish was founded as a result of a promise made to St. Roque by the people of Gokhivare. In 1914 the village was severely affected by an epidemic of cholera. The Catholics made a vow to build a chapel in honor of St. Roque.
Two hundred villagers kept their promise and built a 40’ by 18’ structure to which the Archibishop Lima added a 18’ by 15 Sancury. On June 30, 1930, the Dean of South Bassein blessed the chapel, which was still under the jurisdiction of St, Michael's, Manickpur.
Gokhivare got its independent parish in 1943 with Father Nubiola S. J as the first parish priest. The parish stayed under the care of the Jesuits, except for the brief period between 1968-71 when Fr. Servulo Vaz, a secular priest was the Vicar.
In 1990 the church was extended on the Northern side. However with large migration of Catholics of Mumbai to Vasai, this parish has been completely demolished and built again into a massive structure from scratch.

Gokhivare, Vasai Rd. (E), Dist Thane 401 208
